title: Hilbert's 12th Problem
content: The module docstring introduces Hilbert's 12th Problem (Kronecker's Jugendtraum). It explains the problem status by case: solved for Q (Kronecker-Weber), solved for imaginary quadratic (CM theory), and open for real quadratic and general number fields.
mathContext: The problem asks: given a number field $K$, find explicit analytic functions $f_1, f_2, \ldots$ whose special values $f_i(\alpha_j)$ generate all abelian extensions $L/K$. For $K = \mathbb{Q}$, the answer is the exponential function $e^{2\pi i/n}$ giving roots of unity.

title: Abelian Extensions
content: Defines IsAbelianExtension and AbelianExtension: a field extension L/K that is both Galois and has a commutative Galois group. Also defines cyclotomic extensions via IsCyclotomicExtension.
mathContext: An extension $L/K$ is abelian if $L/K$ is Galois and $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ is abelian. Equivalently, $\sigma \circ \tau = \tau \circ \sigma$ for all $\sigma, \tau \in \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$. Examples: $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})/\mathbb{Q}$ (Gal = $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$), $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q}$ (Gal = $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$).

title: Kronecker-Weber Theorem
content: States the Kronecker-Weber theorem: every finite abelian extension of Q is contained in some cyclotomic field Q(zeta_n). This completely solves Hilbert's 12th problem for K = Q.
mathContext: $L/\mathbb{Q}$ abelian and finite $\Rightarrow \exists n \in \mathbb{N}^+$ and an injection $L \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$. Equivalently, $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}} = \bigcup_n \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$. The proof uses local class field theory at each prime.

title: Cyclotomic Galois Groups are Abelian
content: Proves cyclotomic_galois_comm and cyclotomic_galois_abelian: the Galois group of Q(zeta_n)/Q is commutative. The proof uses IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow to transfer commutativity from (Z/nZ)^x.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)/\mathbb{Q}) \cong (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ via $\sigma \mapsto k$ where $\sigma(\zeta_n) = \zeta_n^k$. Since $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ is abelian, so is the Galois group. The proof: $\sigma\tau = h^{-1}(h(\sigma) \cdot h(\tau)) = h^{-1}(h(\tau) \cdot h(\sigma)) = \tau\sigma$ where $h$ is `autEquivPow`.

title: Cyclotomic Degree
content: Proves cyclotomic_degree: [Q(zeta_n):Q] = phi(n). This follows from the irreducibility of the nth cyclotomic polynomial over Q (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension.finrank).
mathContext: $[\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n):\mathbb{Q}] = \varphi(n) = |\{k : 1 \leq k \leq n, \gcd(k,n) = 1\}|$. This equals the degree of the cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n(x)$, which is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Complex Multiplication
content: Defines IsImaginaryQuadratic, IsRealQuadratic, and CMSolution. For imaginary quadratic K, the CM solution states that j-invariants and torsion points on CM elliptic curves generate all abelian extensions of K.
mathContext: For $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, an elliptic curve $E$ has CM by $\mathcal{O}_K$ if $\mathrm{End}(E) \cong \mathcal{O}_K$. Then $j(E)$ generates the Hilbert class field $H_K$, and the coordinates of $n$-torsion points $E[n]$ generate ray class fields. Together these exhaust $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$.

title: Artin Reciprocity
content: States the Artin reciprocity law: for any number field K, the Artin map gives an isomorphism between the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension and the idele class group. This classifies abelian extensions abstractly but does not give explicit generators.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{ab}}/K) \cong \widehat{C_K} / K^\times$ where $C_K = \mathbb{A}_K^\times / K^\times$ is the idele class group. The Artin map $\psi: C_K \to \mathrm{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{ab}}/K)$ sends each idele to its Frobenius. This is abstract - Hilbert 12 asks for the explicit side.

title: Hilbert's 12th Problem (General)
content: Defines Hilberts12thProblem: for any number field K, find explicit analytic functions whose special values generate all abelian extensions. Proves it is solved for Q (via Kronecker-Weber) and imaginary quadratic fields (via CM theory).
mathContext: The general problem asks for explicit generators $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots$ such that $K^{\mathrm{ab}} = K(\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots)$, where each $\alpha_i$ is a special value of a known analytic function.

title: Concrete Examples
content: Provides concrete Lean examples: Q(i) = CyclotomicField 4, Q(sqrt(-3)) = CyclotomicField 3. Proves cyclotomic_irreducible: the nth cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible over Z (using cyclotomic.irreducible_rat from Mathlib).
mathContext: $\mathbb{Q}(i) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_4)$ since $i = \zeta_4 = e^{2\pi i/4}$. $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3)$ since $\zeta_3 = (-1 + \sqrt{-3})/2$. The irreducibility of $\Phi_n(x)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is a classical result.

title: Stark Conjectures
content: Defines StarkConjecture: predicts that special values of L-functions at s=0 are related to 'Stark units' that generate abelian extensions. For real quadratic fields, Stark units would solve Hilbert's 12th problem.
mathContext: The Stark conjecture predicts: $L'(0, \chi) = -\frac{1}{e_S} \log |\varepsilon_{\chi}^\sigma|$ where $\varepsilon_\chi$ is a 'Stark unit' in the abelian extension cut out by $\chi$, and $e_S$ is a regulator-like factor. These units would explicitly generate abelian extensions.

title: Problem Status Summary
content: Summarizes the complete status of Hilbert's 12th Problem: solved for Q (Kronecker-Weber, 1886) and imaginary quadratic (CM theory), open for real quadratic (Stark conjectures) and general number fields. The fundamental difficulty: class field theory gives abstract classification but not explicit generators.
mathContext: The solved cases use specific analytic functions: $e^{2\pi i z}$ for $\mathbb{Q}$ (roots of unity) and the Weierstrass $\wp$-function/j-invariant for imaginary quadratic fields. No analogous functions are known for real quadratic or general fields.
